name: chokidar-glob-expansion-removed-gulp-watch
behavioral_change: In chokidar v_new (4.0.0), glob expansion was removed: v_old (3.x) let `chokidar.watch` accept glob strings, deriving the directory to traverse with glob-parent and matching files with anymatch, whereas v4 treats the first argument of `watch` as a literal path. The call form is unchanged and no exception is raised; a pattern such as `/w/test/fixtures/**/*.js` is treated as a non-existent path, so the watcher emits no add, change or unlink events.
downstream_effect: gulp-watch resolves the caller's globs to absolute patterns and passes them to `chokidar.watch(globs, options)` in index.js, so after the upgrade the vinyl stream is created and ready fires but no file is ever pushed, and 21 mocha tests time out. The failures give only test file paths and node-internal timer frames plus one frame inside chokidar's own index.js; no line of the downstream index.js or the `chokidar.watch` statement is named.
reference_fix: The reference fix rewrites the `chokidar.watch(globs, options)` call in index.js to watch each pattern's glob-parent root and filter files through an `isIgnored` anymatch predicate that never prunes directories, extracting the existing parent-directory matching into `matchingGlob` and adjusting `outputStream.add` accordingly.
documented_in: The chokidar v4 README at https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar#upgrading contrasts v3 `chok.watch('**/*.js')` with v4 `chok.watch('.', { ignored: (path, stats) => stats?.isFile() && !path.endsWith('.js') })`, and its Changelog section announces `v4 (Sep 2024): remove glob support and bundled fsevents`. The README shows a hard-coded example of the strategy but not the general form used by the reference fix, and the 4.0.0 GitHub release notes say only `Remove glob support` with no code.
